reasons: Lake record identifies Howes v. Fields / Howes, Warden v. Fields, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2012-02-21, docket 10-680.
Lake citations match the page: official 565 U.S. 499; parallels 132 S. Ct. 1181 and 182 L. Ed. 2d 17; vendor cites 2012 U.S. LEXIS 1077 and 2012 WL 538280.
The opinion expressly applies and refines Miranda custody doctrine for prisoner interrogation, rejecting a categorical rule and requiring attention to all features of the interrogation.
The lake record shows SCOTUS status plus substantial progeny data, supporting the editorial 'Key' role for a Miranda custodial-interrogation page.
residual_risks: The exact label 'Key — Progeny / Refinement' is editorial, but the disclosed opinion and lake record support the role at that breadth.

defect.evidence_quote:
Taking into account all of the circumstances of the
questioning—including especially the undisputed fact that
respondent was told that he was free to end the question-
ing and to return to his cell—we hold that respondent was
not in custody within the meaning of Miranda.
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported, but the frontmatter assertion ends with a literal ellipsis after 'here,' and is incomplete as a holding statement.
defect.proposed_fix: Complete the holding: 'Imprisonment alone does not make questioning custodial for Miranda; whether an inmate is in custody depends on all the features of the interrogation, and Fields was not in Miranda custody on these facts.'

reasons: The opinion states that imprisonment alone is not enough to create Miranda custody.
The opinion states that prisoner-custody analysis should focus on all features of the interrogation.
The opinion holds that Fields was not in custody within the meaning of Miranda.
residual_risks: The ellipsis may be an intentional display truncation convention, but in the disclosed built page it appears as the stored holding text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the ellipsis with the actual case-specific outcome.
